title: Siege of Alesia
description: Julius Caesar forces the surrender of Vercingetorix, completing the Roman conquest of Gaul.

title: Baptism of Clovis
description: The king of the Franks is baptised a Catholic by Bishop Remigius; the year is debated and may be as late as 508.

title: Battle of Tours
description: Charles Martel's Franks defeat an Umayyad army from Spain.

title: Normandy granted to Rollo
description: Charles the Simple gives the Viking leader Rollo land on the lower Seine, the origin of the duchy of Normandy.

title: Hugh Capet becomes king
description: The election of Hugh Capet begins the Capetian dynasty, whose branches rule France until 1848.

title: Council of Clermont
description: Pope Urban II calls on the knights of the West to go to the aid of the Christians of the East, launching the First Crusade.

title: Building of Notre-Dame begins
description: Work starts on the cathedral of Paris, largely complete by 1260.

title: Battle of Bouvines
description: Philip II defeats the emperor Otto IV and the allies of King John, confirming the French crown's hold on Normandy and Anjou.

title: Papacy moves to Avignon
description: Pope Clement V settles at Avignon, where the popes stay until 1376.

title: Battle of Crécy
description: Edward III's archers defeat a larger French army early in the Hundred Years' War.

title: Joan of Arc relieves Orléans
description: The English lift their siege, the turning point of the Hundred Years' War.

title: Battle of Castillon
description: French artillery destroys the last English army in Gascony, the final battle of the Hundred Years' War.

title: Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts
description: Francis I requires legal and official documents to be written in French in place of Latin.

title: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre
description: Catholic mobs and royal troops kill thousands of Huguenots in Paris and then in the provinces.

title: Edict of Nantes
description: Henry IV grants the Huguenots freedom of worship in set places, ending the Wars of Religion.

title: Louis XIV becomes king
description: A four-year-old begins a reign of 72 years, the longest of any European monarch.

title: Edict of Nantes revoked
description: Louis XIV outlaws Protestant worship, and more than 200,000 Huguenots leave France.

title: Storming of the Bastille
description: Parisians take the royal fortress and prison, the event that came to stand for the French Revolution.

title: Declaration of the Rights of Man
description: The National Constituent Assembly adopts a statement of liberty, equality before the law and the sovereignty of the nation.

title: Monarchy abolished
description: The National Convention ends the monarchy, and the First Republic dates from the next day.

title: Execution of Louis XVI
description: The former king is guillotined after the Convention convicts him of treason.

title: Fall of Robespierre
description: The Convention turns on Robespierre, who is guillotined the next day, ending the Terror.

title: Coup of 18 Brumaire
description: Napoleon Bonaparte overthrows the Directory and takes power as First Consul.

title: Napoleon crowned emperor
description: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

title: July Revolution
description: Three days of fighting in Paris replace Charles X with Louis-Philippe.

title: February Revolution
description: Louis-Philippe abdicates and the Second Republic is proclaimed, the spark for revolutions across Europe.

title: Battle of Sedan
description: Napoleon III and his army surrender to the Prussians, and the Third Republic is proclaimed in Paris two days later.

title: Paris Commune
description: A revolutionary government takes over Paris for two months until the army crushes it in the Bloody Week.

title: Separation of church and state
description: The law ends state funding and recognition of religion, the basis of French secularism.

title: First Battle of the Marne
description: French and British armies stop the German advance on Paris, and the western front settles into trenches.

title: Battle of Verdun begins
description: A German offensive opens ten months of fighting that costs the two armies more than 700,000 casualties.

title: Armistice of 11 November
description: Germany signs the armistice in Marshal Foch's railway carriage, ending the fighting on the western front.

title: Treaty of Versailles
description: Germany signs the peace treaty in the Hall of Mirrors, accepting losses of territory, disarmament and reparations.

title: Armistice with Germany
description: Six weeks after the German attack France signs an armistice; the north and west are occupied and a government at Vichy rules the rest.

title: Liberation of Paris
description: The German garrison surrenders to French and American troops and the Resistance.

title: Fall of Dien Bien Phu
description: The Viet Minh take the French fortress, ending French rule in Indochina.

title: Fifth Republic founded
description: A new constitution with a strong presidency, written for Charles de Gaulle during the Algerian crisis, comes into force.

title: Évian Accords
description: France and the Algerian National Liberation Front agree a ceasefire, and Algeria becomes independent in July.

title: May 1968
description: Student protests and a general strike of about ten million workers shake de Gaulle's government.

title: Paris attacks
description: Islamic State gunmen and bombers kill 130 people at the Bataclan theatre, cafés and the national stadium.
